body:
Ref #130459

## Relationship to #130460

This is **complementary to, not overlapping with, @waterWang's #130460**.

Issue #130459 reports two distinct defects. #130460 correctly fixes the first
(the `AddMany` write-back that produced `annotation_id = 0` rows) and I've
confirmed that fix independently in a review comment there. This PR fixes the
second — the issue's unresolved item 5, the unsatisfiable `DELETE` — which
#130460 does not touch.

The two changes are in different functions and share no lines, so they can land
in either order, independently.

## The bug

In `ensureTags`:

```go
sess.MustCols("annotation_id", "tag_id").In("tag_id", tagsDelete).
    Delete(annotationTag{AnnotationID: annotationID})
```

The bean's `TagID` is zero, and `MustCols` exists precisely to force zero-valued
columns into generated SQL — `engine_cond.go:69` honours `mustColumnMap` when
building conditions. So `tag_id` landed in the `WHERE` clause **twice**:

```sql
DELETE FROM annotation_tag
WHERE tag_id IN ($1 … $n) AND annotation_id = $n+1 AND tag_id = $n+2  -- bound to 0
```

`tag_id IN (...) AND tag_id = 0` is unsatisfiable, so the delete matched zero
rows. Tags removed from an annotation were never unlinked, and stale
`annotation_tag` rows accumulated for every annotation whose tags ever changed.
All three callers are affected — `Add`, `update` and `AddMany`.

This is the malformed statement the issue reports verbatim as item 5. The
~46,900-bind `IN` list there was amplified by the `AddMany` bug (`annotation_id = 0`
matched all 47k orphans, so `tagsDelete` was enormous), but the dead
`AND tag_id = 0` predicate is present on every call regardless.

## The fix

Drop `tag_id` from `MustCols`. `annotation_id` stays listed deliberately: without
it, a zero annotation ID would be omitted from the condition entirely and widen
the delete to every row matching `tag_id IN (...)`.

## Why the existing tests didn't catch this

`Get` builds `ItemDTO.Tags` from the denormalized `annotation.tags` column, so
`Can update annotation and remove all tags` and its siblings were green while the
join table was wrong. `GetTags` — which powers annotation tag filtering — joins
`annotation_tag`, and therefore returned tags the annotation no longer had. That
is the user-visible symptom.

## Test

Extended `Can update annotation with additional tags` in `TestIntegrationAnnotations`
to query the join table directly, since the existing `items[0].Tags` assertion
reads the denormalized column and cannot see the stale row. The subtest replaces
`newtag2` with `newtag3`, so `newtag2`'s link must be gone.

Without the fix:

```
--- FAIL: TestIntegrationAnnotations/.../Can_update_annotation_with_additional_tags
    extra elements in list B:
    Messages: replaced tags must be deleted from annotation_tag, not just from annotation.tags
```

With the fix:

```
go test ./pkg/services/annotations/... -count=1
ok  pkg/services/annotations/accesscontrol            1.660s
ok  pkg/services/annotations/annotationsapi            4.457s
ok  pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl          11.375s
ok  pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/loki      6.608s
```

Verified fail-before/pass-after on this branch alone, with the `AddMany` bug still
present — the two are independent.

`go build`, `go vet` and `gofmt` clean on `./pkg/services/annotations/...`.

## Not included

Cleanup of already-accumulated stale rows. `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` already
exists and handles rows whose annotation is gone, though not stale links to
annotations that still exist. A data migration felt out of scope for a correctness
fix — happy to add one if maintainers want existing installations repaired on
upgrade.
title: Annotations: fix ensureTags never deleting removed tag links
